frozen_decisions_applied: FD-01/FD-02 (unchanged from the committed foundation): core::DeviceId canonical identity; service owns the locator registry.

Plan Section 7.2 remap algorithm steps 1-5 (DeviceLocatorRegistry::remap) are now actually invoked from ZigbeeLifecycleCoordinator::handle_join_candidate() before every kDeviceJoined event, closing the gap between 'implemented and tested in isolation' and 'load-bearing in the Service runtime'.

S2 required change #6/#7: hal_zigbee_callbacks_t now carries EUI-64 for join/leave; the real ESP-Zigbee (ESP_PLATFORM) path's existing internal IEEE-address table (s_known_device_identities, notify_join_with_identity) now has its already-resolved address threaded through to the callback instead of being discarded after synthesizing a legacy leave/join pair.

S2 required change #9/#10: inbound short-address reports/results are now resolved to DeviceId (via DeviceLocatorRegistry) before reaching Core, for every event-construction site discovered in this stage (join, leave, interview, bind, configure-reporting, attribute report, raw attribute report, Tuya-translated telemetry).

hal_callback_extension.status: COMPLETE, HOST-COMPILED AND TESTED; ESP_PLATFORM branch written by inspection, NOT compiled/verified
hal_callback_extension.detail: hal_zigbee_callbacks_t::on_device_joined/on_device_left gained a third `const uint8_t* ieee_addr` parameter (NULL = unresolved). This is the one genuinely breaking signature change in this stage. Backward compatibility for every other caller was preserved by keeping hal_zigbee_notify_device_joined(short_addr)/hal_zigbee_simulate_device_joined(short_addr) (and _left) at their ORIGINAL signatures, reimplemented as thin wrappers around new hal_zigbee_notify/simulate_device_{joined,left}_with_identity(short_addr, ieee_addr) siblings. Two test/target/*.c files that implement the callback struct fields directly (test_reporting_flow.c, test_hal_zigbee.c) needed their local callback signatures updated; all other test/target/*.c/.cpp files call the unchanged-signature notify functions and needed no change. None of test/target/ compiles in this environment (BLOCKED_TOOLCHAIN, no ESP-IDF/esp-zigbee-lib).

real_stack_path.detail: hal_zigbee.c's real ESP-Zigbee signal handlers (device-associated, device-annce, device-update, leave-indication) already extracted an IEEE address from esp_zb_* signal params and passed it to notify_join_with_identity()/notify_left_with_identity() before this change -- that address is now threaded one level further, through notify_join_with_source()/notify_left_with_source(), into the callback. No new esp_zb_* SDK calls were added. This is the part of the change with the highest real-world risk of a subtle error (in particular, the IEEE-address byte order assumed when building core::DeviceId in hal_event_adapter.cpp's build_device_id_from_ieee() is UNVERIFIED against real hardware/SDK documentation -- see the code comment there) and requires a target build plus HIL/device test before being trusted in production.

service_layer_wiring.detail: ServiceRuntime now owns a DeviceLocatorRegistry instance (device_locator_registry_ member, public device_locator_registry() accessor, public resolve_device_id_for_short_addr() helper). ZigbeeLifecycleCoordinator::handle_join_candidate() calls DeviceLocatorRegistry::remap() (the full displacement-aware algorithm) before constructing the kDeviceJoined CoreEvent. post_zigbee_interview_result/bind_result/configure_reporting_result, the legacy on_attribute_report path, post_zigbee_attribute_report_raw (all 7 internal event constructions: LQI/RSSI/temperature/occupancy/contact/battery telemetry) and try_tuya_translate all now resolve device_id from the registry via short_addr before posting into Core, so every currently-implemented Zigbee event type carries a resolved identity once a device has joined with one.

end_to_end_test.detail: test/host/test_service_device_identity_wiring.cpp exercises the full chain via hal_zigbee_simulate_device_joined_with_identity()/_left_with_identity() (public HAL test-mock entry points, not internal APIs) and proves, without touching Core or the registry directly: a resolved join creates exactly one record; DeviceLocatorRegistry and Core's view agree; interview/bind/configure-reporting results land on the SAME record; a short-address remap for the same identity updates the locator only (INV-ID-01, no lifecycle reset); a different identity joining does not inherit reporting state (INV-ID-02/03); leave marks the registry entry offline (not erased -- diagnostic breadcrumb, per FD-15-adjacent design intent) and removes the Core record.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: core_reducer.cpp's short_addr fallback for identity-less events (documented in the original S2 manifest) is UNCHANGED and still present.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: It remains correct and necessary: it is what keeps command-result/network-status event paths (which never carry device identity by design -- they are correlation-id-scoped, not device-scoped) and any future not-yet-updated call site safe. This stage's work populates device_id at every CURRENTLY discovered device-scoped event-construction site; the fallback is the safety net for anything not yet found, not a shortcut that was supposed to be removed.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.invariant_preservation: Unchanged from the original manifest: a record with a valid device_id can never be matched/mutated by a short_addr-only event. Re-verified by test_service_device_identity_wiring.cpp under the now-live wiring, not just by the standalone reducer test.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: The real ESP_PLATFORM hal_zigbee.c IEEE-address byte order used when constructing core::DeviceId (components/service/hal_event_adapter.cpp: build_device_id_from_ieee) is an unverified assumption (bytes taken as-is, matching this file's existing un-reversed IEEE-address logging convention).
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: No ESP-IDF/esp-zigbee-lib toolchain or real hardware is available in this environment to confirm esp_zb_ieee_addr_t's actual byte order against the EUI-64 canonical (MSB-first) text-form convention core::DeviceId uses.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: If wrong, persisted-later DeviceIds would not visually match a device's printed IEEE address, though internal consistency (same device always maps to the same DeviceId) would still hold since the conversion is deterministic and used uniformly. Documented as the single specific item needing hardware confirmation before production trust, in docs/architecture/DEVICE_IDENTITY.md Section 3.1 and in the conversion function's own code comment (the only place the fix would need to be made).
